items_missed: No "How are you today?" in the greeting
No agenda statement ("I'll gather some details, then walk through pricing, takes about 10-15 minutes") and no explicit "Sound good?" confirmation before diving in
Never asked about additional rooms/storage, extra stops, or access concerns (elevator/parking) - customer had to volunteer the freight-elevator reservation himself
Never asked "Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?"
No "Pricing is super simple" opener before quoting the rate
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000)
Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee (discount if the arrival window is missed)
No sense-check ("Does that make sense?") after explaining the clock/billing increments
Didn't factor in or explain elevator wait time / walk distance as a variable for this 36th-floor move
Save Your Ass speech hit the core "prep = shorter move = lower bill" message but skipped concrete consolidation examples, the "take a carload" tip, and a closing "does that make sense?"
Didn't mention the bolded detail list in the confirmation email or ask the customer to reply with corrections
No specific office hours or contact info given - only a vague "feel free to contact us"
Never used the customer's first name (Binu) once during the entire call
top_strength: Built genuine, specific rapport by recalling and reminiscing about the customer's previous movers by name and description (Robert, Peter), and closed with a clear itemized rate/estimate breakdown ($208/hr, 3.25-4.25 hr range, $676-$884) that got the move booked in an efficient 8.5-minute call.
coaching_note: Finish the full room/access probe (elevator wait, extra stops, additional rooms) before quoting pricing - on this call Nick priced out a 36th-floor high-rise move without ever asking about elevator or access conditions, which is exactly the kind of gap that drives estimate-vs-actual misses.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, easy rapport (recalling the customer's previous movers by name) and a personal farewell keep energy positive throughout, though the pricing/estimate explanation gets rambly and script-heavy in the middle.
